analysis: The supplied units are base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md. The PR modifies only this documentation file, around base line 453 and later head ranges. The patch excerpt is incomplete, but the visible head hunk (head 453-473) adds prose on cluster onboarding stop handling. It describes a stopsAsked counter in ClusterSetupRecord, a count carried in ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked, and followers ending the wait when the count grows. No executable code, build scripts, configuration or wire-format changes are visible, so no security regression is evident from the supplied evidence. Relevant threat IDs are none directly. The described behavior touches the cluster control/status path and the stop lifecycle, which are loosely related to T-059 and T-060 (availability) and TB-012 (local add-on hold). It does not touch the TB-002 coordinator-to-provider WebSocket, attestation (TB-009, TB-011), prefix-cache storage (T-041) or key custody. One integration question remains for any code change that accompanies this documentation. A peer-reported stopsAsked count could be forged by an unauthenticated or compromised follower to force the leader's onboarding wait to end. The doc states that status replies come over the authenticated pair control link, and the code is not supplied here, so the claim is unverified. The remaining head hunks (head 3239-3242 and 3255-3286) are not visible in the supplied units, so they are a coverage limit and not evidence of safety. The T-041 sections are unchanged and the doc's cache claims are not altered in the visible text.
